title: Design System: Paula Gallucci Zurita — Questfolio

title.purpose: Section headers and card titles (project, achievement names).

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked micro-labels on stat cards.

data.purpose: Monospace numeric readouts (XP, hours, counts) on stat cards.

shadows.name: glow
shadows.purpose: Retired. Was a cyan bloom on the hero avatar and primary CTAs; removed in the Quiet Signal revision. Kept as a schema field resolving to no shadow.

shadows.name: sm
shadows.purpose: Reserved for low-emphasis lift; not used by a shipped component.

shadows.name: md
shadows.purpose: Reserved for future overlay-style surfaces (dropdowns, popovers).

shadows.name: lg
shadows.purpose: Reserved for modal-level surfaces that need to lift off the page.

motion.name: duration-base
motion.purpose: Default state-change transition (card hover, nav active state).

motion.name: cursor-spring
motion.purpose: Spring inertia on the cursor-trail dot's position.

zIndex.name: cursor
zIndex.purpose: Cursor-trail dot — always renders above everything else.

lightMode.note: Not a naive inversion. Every color used as text/icon/small-fill is independently re-tuned in OKLCH (same hue, different lightness) to clear 4.5:1 against every light surface — see DESIGN.md section 2, 'Light Mode'.

components.html: View projects

components.name: Cursor Dot
components.description: New signature component. A small Signal Cyan dot that trails the real cursor with spring inertia; grows and brightens over interactive elements. Absent on touch devices and under reduced motion.
components.css: .ds-cursor-dot { position: fixed; left: 0; top: 0; width: 24px; height: 24px; border-radius: 9999px; background: #22d3ee; opacity: 0.5; transform: translate(-50%, -50%) scale(0.35); pointer-events: none; transition: transform 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1), opacity 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); z-index: 60; } .ds-cursor-dot--active { opacity: 0.85; transform: translate(-50%, -50%) scale(1); }

narrative.overview: The portfolio was "The Cyber Nebula": three neon signal colors and a cyan glow against a blue-violet-tinted void. This revision strips that back to one instrument, dialed low. The background, surfaces, borders, and text are now nearly grayscale — the same cool undertone as before, but pulled down to a whisper of chroma rather than a visible tint. Against that quiet field, exactly one color still fires: Signal Cyan. No glow bloom carries it anymore; the color itself, used sparingly, is the whole signal. Violet and magenta didn't disappear — they're still present as barely-there dusty echoes in case anything ever needs a second neutral-ish tone, but they no longer read as "color" to a viewer. Corners are uniformly 3px everywhere in the system — not the sharp 0px of a terminal, not the soft 10-18px pill language of a generic SaaS product, but a single quiet value repeated without variation. A small cyan dot trails the real cursor with a touch of spring inertia: the one deliberately alive, playful gesture in an otherwise very quiet system. This system explicitly rejects the generic SaaS-neon-gradient look, and also rejects its own former self: no bloom, no multi-color signal chorus, no soft varied radius scale.
keyCharacteristics: Near-monochrome neutrals (background, surface, border, text) — the same cool undertone as before, chroma reduced to a whisper
Exactly one active color in the whole system: Signal Cyan. No shadow-based glow anywhere
One uniform 3px corner radius everywhere — no scale, no pills, no sharp 0px terminal look either
A small cyan cursor-trail dot with spring inertia is the system's one overtly playful gesture, always paired with a native, visible cursor
Locked or pending content stays visible as grayscale + dashed border — curiosity over absence
Motion is quick and functional (120-420ms); the cursor dot is the one place spring easing is used, and only there

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Signal Cyan is the only color in the system allowed to read as "color" to a viewer. Violet and magenta exist only as muted, near-gray echoes held in reserve. Status colors and achievement tiers are functional, not brand color, and are the only other exception.

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: Nothing in this system casts a colored shadow. Presence is carried by the color and the geometry themselves, at rest, not by a bloom that appears on top of them.

rules.name: The One Heading Font Rule
rules.body: Space Grotesk is the only typeface used for anything that names or labels a section or entity — headings, titles, nav items, the profile name. Inter is reserved for sentences; JetBrains Mono is reserved for numbers.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: No component gets a shadow just for being a container, and no component gets a shadow for being important either. Shadows are reserved for genuine overlay surfaces that lift off the page.

rules.name: The Re-Lit, Not Inverted Rule
rules.body: Light mode is not background: white with every color otherwise untouched. Any color used as text, an icon, or a small fill must be re-tuned per mode to clear contrast — same hue, different lightness — never assumed to carry over from dark mode unchanged.

dos: Do treat Signal Cyan as the only color that reads as "color" — everything else is a near-gray neutral, a muted echo, or a functional status/tier color.
Do keep every corner in the system at the same 3px radius — the uniformity is the point, not the specific value.
Do use a 1px Quiet Line border, never a shadow, to separate any surface from Quiet Void.
Do keep the cursor dot subtle and skip it entirely on touch devices and under reduced motion.
Do render locked or pending content as grayscale + dashed border, never simply omit it — the point is curiosity, not absence.
Do keep Space Grotesk for anything that names a section or entity, Inter for sentences, and JetBrains Mono for numbers — never blend the three within one text block.
Do re-tune any new color for light mode independently in theme.light.json — same hue, a lightness that actually clears contrast.
donts: Don't use gradient-clip text, glassmorphism panels, or purple-to-pink hero blobs — the generic SaaS-neon-dashboard look this system explicitly rejects.
Don't add a glow, bloom, or any colored shadow to any element, no matter how important — this system explicitly retired that move.
Don't use a soft varied radius scale (4/10/18px-style pills and rounded cards) — one radius, everywhere.
Don't reactivate the muted secondary/tertiary echoes at full saturation.
Don't fill a badge with a solid color — the 10%-opacity tint is the badge.
Don't ship a light-mode color that's a naive white-background inversion without checking contrast — Signal Cyan alone drops from 10.6:1 to 1.7:1 doing that.
Don't round a stat card's corners — its square edge is what marks it as a data tile, now the system's one deliberate exception.
Don't hide the native cursor or make any interaction depend on the cursor dot being visible — it's decorative, not functional.
Don't add bounce/elastic easing or celebratory motion (confetti, cartoon pop-ins) to achievement unlocks — the tone is earned and quiet, never toy-like.
